Maria: Heads-up — we're hitting a TP all-reduce bottleneck on the dedicated cluster for small/medium message sizes. Landing the kernel selection tweak yesterday seems correlated with a perf regression on TP jobs.

Alex: Can you paste the microbench results you ran?

Maria: Pasted quick nccl-tests numbers below (same 8-GPU TP topology, p3dn-like network):
```
# nccl-tests allReduce microbench (8 ranks, measured avg latency us)
msg_size    ring_us    tree_us
512B         120        95
2KB          140       110
16KB         260       240
64KB         480       300
256KB        900       320
1MB         2200      700
```

Maria: Also captured a short nvprof/nccl profiling snapshot from a failing run: comm stalls dominate during forward KV cache syncs, ~45% timeline is NCCL wait vs ~30% compute.

Sam: Interesting — tree wins for >~32-64KB, ring better for sub-1KB. What's the message-size distribution coming out of our TP chunking/kv-sync?

Maria: We observed many intermediate tensors around 16–64KB due to the new kernel tiling; previously we had more 256KB+ fused grads. The kernel change reduced per-op compute but increased # of allreduce calls.

Toni: So regression = higher #small-to-mid messages => ring performs poorly in mid-range due to O(N) latency accumulation across the ring. Tree reduces the hop-count for larger messages. Also suspect we aren't overlapping comm and compute effectively after the kernel refactor.

Alex: Do we call async ops / schedule overlaps? Example snippet we're using now: `torch.distributed.all_reduce(tensor, op=dist.ReduceOp.SUM, async_op=False)` — that's synchronous on the CPU side.

Sam: Try `async_op=True` and queueing work with `req.wait()` deferred, or use `torch.cuda.stream()` to push compute onto a separate stream. Also consider increasing fusion threshold to reduce number of calls.

Maria: Quick experiment notes I ran locally: enabling async_op + stream overlap reduced NCCL wait from 45% -> ~25% for the 16KB/64KB regime, but introduced some CUDA stream ordering bugs in a couple of ops (tracked in #PR-458).

Toni: Another lever: switch NCCL algorithm selection. Env vars we should try in CI: `NCCL_ALGO=Tree`, `NCCL_ALGO=Ring`, `NCCL_MAX_RINGS=4`, and `NCCL_MIN_NRINGS=1`. Also experiment with `NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=0/1` and `NCCL_BUFFSIZE`.

Alex: For us, practical config changes: (1) increase `tensor_fusion_threshold` from 64KB -> 256KB for TP paths; (2) enable comm/compute overlap in the runtime for KV syncs; (3) add dynamic algo selection in our TP scheduler: if mean_msg_size > 64KB prefer tree.

Maria: I ran a short A/B on dedicated cluster (canary):
```
A: default (ring, fusion 64KB)  -> mean step latency = 1230 ms
B: tree + fusion 256KB -> mean step latency = 820 ms
```
B had 33% end-to-end improvement on that workload.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout to `dedicated-us-west-2` started at 2024-04-08T15:20Z (job id rded-20240408-99).

Sam: Nice. We should be careful: tree requires different peer-ordering and might regress for tiny messages (e.g., embedding lookups). So make dynamic selection the default path instead of global switch.

Toni: Agree. Also log histogram of allreduce message sizes in production so we can pick thresholds empirically per-customer. Add a runtime flag `--tp-comm-algo=auto|ring|tree` that defaults to `auto`.

Maria: I've opened internal ticket infra#2102 with measurement artifacts and the nccl traces attached. Next steps: @Sam to land async overlap branch + add histogram logging; @Toni to prototype `tp-comm-algo=auto` with simple threshold heuristic; I'll run full perf sweep on canary for 3 more models.

Alex: Ping me once you have perf numbers, I'll prepare a short playbook for on-call (how to flip algo, env var list, rollback steps).

Maria: One more note — kernel selection tweak we shipped yesterday reduced compute by ~12% but increased #of ops; will revert or change to fuse more aggressively if we can't get comm overlap stable. :thinking:

Sam: Cool. I'll start the async overlap PR and post benchmarks in this thread. :+1:

Toni: I'll add the histogram logging and a dashboard tile in the console (per-model TP allreduce size distribution).

Maria: Thanks team — filing meeting to review post-canary results next Wed.
